profile.campus: Vantage San Antonio Campus (Texas Research Park)
profile.reading:
This building, mapped a second time in this registry as TX12, is located at 17420 Omicron Drive in the Texas Research Park area of San Antonio, TX; this is a duplicate OSM point for the same TX12 building tracked elsewhere in this registry under a separate way ID, rather than a distinct sixth San Antonio facility. Vantage does not publish this campus on its own site at all, so this entry relies on secondary sourcing: Data Center Dynamics reporting on the building permit. TX12 was filed for permit in October 2025 at a stated construction cost of roughly $276.8 million, covering approximately 432,800 square feet across two stories with up to 96 megawatts of power, with a construction timeline running from October 2025 to August 2027.

Vantage acquired 57.9 acres on Omicron/Theta Drive from the University of Texas System Board of Regents in July 2023, and a separate 31 acres at State Highway 151/Wiseman Boulevard in August 2023, forming two San Antonio sub-campuses: Texas Research Park (Omicron Drive, home to TX11 and TX12) and Westover Hills (Rogers Road/Wiseman Boulevard, home to TX21 and TX22). This San Antonio campus is distinct from Vantage's much larger "Frontier" mega-campus, a separate $25 billion, 1.4-gigawatt, 3.7-million-square-foot, 1,200-acre development in rural Shackelford County, Texas, announced in August 2025 to meet AI demand.

San Antonio's data center growth, including Vantage's TX cluster, has concentrated on the city's West and Northwest sides where CPS Energy, the nation's largest municipally owned combined electric and gas utility, has courted large industrial and data center loads with dedicated substations and negotiated rate agreements. Bexar County and the City of San Antonio have both offered property-tax abatement agreements to data center developers as part of a broader economic-diversification push beyond the city's traditional military and tourism base. This OSM point duplicates another mapped point for the same TX12 building elsewhere in this dataset; both are retained here since each corresponds to a distinct upstream map feature, but they should be understood as referring to one physical Vantage building rather than two separate facilities. CPS Energy's integrated resource plan and ERCOT have both cited data centers as a fast-growing large-load category driving new transmission and generation investment across San Antonio through the early 2030s.

reading.body:
This building is filed for 96 megawatts of IT capacity across 432,800 square feet, which at typical AI training density of 40 kilowatts per rack implies roughly 2,400 racks. The facility is under construction with a timeline from October 2025 to August 2027 and has not yet published specifications on its own operator website, so capacity figures rest on secondary reporting of building permits. It is one of two mapped buildings at the Texas Research Park sub-campus in San Antonio, distinct from Vantage's separate Frontier mega-campus announced in August 2025 for Shackelford County.

This campus ranks outside the top 18 published data center capacity sites in Texas despite its scale, because most of Texas's 133 mapped facilities do not publish power figures. The state's 18 published sites total 468 megawatts, and this single building would represent 20 percent of that published base, though it remains in planning phase. San Antonio has concentrated data center growth on its West and Northwest sides where CPS Energy, a municipally owned utility, has offered dedicated substations and negotiated rates, alongside property tax abatements from city and county authorities.

CPS Energy and ERCOT have both identified data centers as a fast-growing load driver across San Antonio through the early 2030s, signaling that grid operators expect this facility to claim transmission and generation resources as it comes online. The campus does not yet appear in Vantage's public spec portfolio, making its actual timeline and final capacity contingent on construction progress and permitting.
